title: Managing his father's restaurant at Biriato Beach
summary: His father ran an open-air restaurant near the Casino Nacional in Marianao, with Machito as administrator.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: All right. Okay. You got a job. Your father bought a restaurant? Where?
At the Biriato Beach, that was a private a private......
What beach?
Biriato.
How do you spell that?

Biriato - B-i-R-i-a-t-o, Biriato. He was an architect, and he was very rich because he was in sympathy with Machado and he build, he made a replica of the castle, the Morro Castle of Havana with all the entrances and everything. It was just like Havana Bay in Marianao.
Okay, where was this beach at? This restaurant? Where? What part of Cuba?
Near the Casino, Casin Nacional.
In Havana.
In Marianao.
In Marianao. Okay, tell me about it. Describe the restaurant to me.

Well, we had like a - like a regular, let's say like a regular store. Like we had kitchen and then we had tables in open air, open-air tables and we had the other half covered by - by - you know, by the roof or whatever, and we used to sell rice and beans and tasajo, aporrea, the salty meat with hot sauces and sausages and .....
About how many people, about how many tables did you have?
Well, we could seat about fifty people.
I see. Now, your father was the owner?
Yeah.
And you were what?
I was the administrator.
Okay. You didn't have to wait tables or anything like that?
No.
How many people worked for you?
We had about four fellows, we had two cooks and everything and we sell liquors.
Okay. How did you like being administrator?
Well, it was beautiful, you know, I had a tremendous time. I was a young kid.
And you didn't sing.
No, I was completely retired. I was--that's when the Casino le la Playa started.
I see.
